messages.subject: y-values in a bar plot
parts:
Hi,
I want to use qqplot2 to make a barplot, where to bars are put on top
of each other
I have a dataframe with 3 columns.
1. which defines the x-axis in the barplot
2. defines y-values
3. defines which group (which of the two bars on top of each other)
the values belongs to.

But for some reason I alwas get the y-value to be 1, beacause the
count is 1, but thats because I already calculated this value.
Can anyone help?

messages.subject: Re: y-values in a bar plot
parts:
Your data or dummy data and the code you use to make your graph would make it a lot easier to figure out where things are going wrong. 

I'm assuming your code looks like the following?

ggplot(data= dataframewith3columns, aes(x=xdata, y=ydata, fill=groupvariable)+
geom_bar()

Brandon

frequency1<-c(0.2,0.5,0.6,0.9)
frequency2<-1-frequency1
frequency3<-(frequency1 +frequency2)

Each of these bars should be divided lowest part i red representing
the frequency of good behavior, and upper part in blue representing
bad behavior.
I have tried many times, but R always uses count as y-value, so each
bar has the hight of 2.

messages.author: b3ca0c52e87f982f
messages.subject: Re: y-values in a bar plot
parts:
Hi,

are you sure the mock data you sent reflect what you want? Your
frequency3 variable is always 1 (= frequency 1 +1 - frequency1). I
suppose this is not what you intended.

Anyway, I slighty modified your data to make frequency3 closer to your
description (a frequency), and made a plot that seems to be what you
expected. Let us know if this is not the case.

x <- rep(c('A','B','C','D'), 4)
behavior <- rep(c('Good','Bad'), each=4)

frequency3 <- c(frequency1, frequency2) # Here is the only
modification to your code
data <- data.frame(x,frequency3,behavior2)

# now we plot
ggplot(aes(x=x, y=frequency3, fill=behavior2), data=data) + geom_bar()

Best,

Matthieu

Matthieu Dubois
Post Doctoral Fellow
Psychology Department, ULB
